The tiddler stays one tiddler; no helper tiddlers are created. ## Features - **Toggle per tiddler** - an *outline* button in the view toolbar. Off means the normal view. - **Same rendering** - the tiddler renders exactly as usual; outline mode only adds data attributes, a selection frame and key handling. - **Units** - list items, lists, headings (with sections), paragraphs, code blocks, tables, opened HTML containers, transclusion lines, and widgets or macro calls (one opaque unit each). - **Type badges** - a small, faint label next to every unit shows what it is (paragraph, h2, code-block, bullet, ...), also on the editor field; they take no space. Settings: all (default), headings only, off. - **Selection** - click, Up/Down, Left/Right to the parent / first child, Escape clears. - **Move** - Alt-Up/Alt-Down swap a unit with its sibling, subtree included. Headings and blocks also move across heading lines: a new heading moves up over the blocks above it, a paragraph moves into the next section. - **Indent** - Tab/Shift-Tab demote/promote list items and headings with their subtrees. - **In-place editor** - Enter or a double-click opens TW's own edit widget at the unit: a compact one-line field by default, optionally the full editor with toolbar. Lists and headings are edited without their marker; nesting stays with Tab/Shift-Tab. Ctrl-Enter saves, Enter saves and starts a new unit, Escape discards, Ctrl-Up/Down save and move the editor to the previous/next unit, Alt-Enter turns the unit into another type. In selection mode Ctrl-Enter starts a new empty unit below the selection. - **Delete** - the Delete key removes the selection with everything below it, after a small yes/no menu (a heading: with its section or just the heading); list items without sub-items go at once (a setting). - **Copy, cut, paste** - Ctrl-C, Ctrl-X, Ctrl-V move a unit with its subtree, also to another tiddler; through the system clipboard: formatted into e-mail or Jira, as wikitext into text fields; pasted into an outline a unit takes the level of the place. - **Undo** - Ctrl-Z takes back the last changes made in the outline (deletes, moves, merges, splits, edits), Ctrl-Y redoes them; for the running session. In the editor too, as long as nothing is typed (after a split, merge or move from the editor). - **Split and merge** - Enter in the middle of a list item splits it at the caret, at the start of a filled item or paragraph it opens an empty one above; Backspace at the start of an item joins it to the item above (an empty item is deleted), Delete at its end pulls the item below up, like in Streams. - **Block menu** - Alt-Enter (also in the editor, to turn the edited unit into another type): insert a new paragraph, heading, list, quote or code block after or before the selection (in an empty tiddler: the first block), or turn the selection into another type. - **Key overview** - press `?` in an outline (or its small ? button) for a table of all keys; the *keys* tab shows the same. Every key is configurable in the settings tab with TW's shortcut editor. - **Transclusions** - a marker on `{{...}}` lines; Enter opens the target in outline mode. - **Safe writes** - every write is a splice of a known range; changed text is relocated or refused, never guessed. ## Prerequisites - TiddlyWiki 5.4.0 or later (JS modules: server restart or reload needed after install) - Optional: `rimir/theme`, `rimir/doc-template` ## Quick Start 1. Install the plugin and restart the server. 2. Open a wikitext tiddler and press *outline* in its view toolbar. 3. Click a block; Up/Down select, Alt-Down moves, Tab indents. 4. Enter edits, Ctrl-Enter saves. 5. `?` shows all keys. Wikitext only; Markdown is not supported yet. llm-inline `AI:` lines do not fire from outline edits. $tiddler="$:/plugins/rimir/doc-template/templates/page"> <$fill $name="body"> !! Approach The tiddler is rendered unchanged. A JS widget, `$outline`, wraps the normal body transclusion, walks the rendered widget tree and stamps `data-ol-*` attributes on the DOM node of each unit. One delegated `keydown` and `click` handler lives on the widget's container. Operations are splices of known text ranges. Wrapper elements inside the body are avoided on purpose: they would change the HTML and break CSS such as `ul > li`. The one exception is the widget's own container: while outline mode is on, the whole body sits inside `div.rr-ol-frame > div.rr-ol` (the frame also holds the key overview), so selectors such as `.tc-tiddler-body > p` no longer match (use `.tc-tiddler-body p` or also match `.tc-tiddler-body > .rr-ol-frame > .rr-ol > p`). !! Parts |!File |!Role | |`model.js` |Collects units from the widget tree: start, end, kind, level, parent, siblings | |`text-utils.js`, `dom-utils.js` |Pure text helpers; DOM lookup shared by widget and editor | |`formats.js` |Registry of format adapters | |`format-wikitext.js` |Wikitext adapter: indent, promote, move (siblings, and across heading lines), replace, insertNew, insertBlock (after / before / at the end), convert, remove, deleteUnit, merge, split, editSource, isMultiline | |`outline-widget.js` |The `$outline` widget: unit-to-DOM mapping, stamps, selection, writes | |`outline-keys.js` |Key dispatch through `$:/config/shortcuts/outline-*`; toggles the key overview | |`keys/*`, `ui/keys-table`, `keys.tid` |Key groups (caption, hint, list of shortcut names), the overview table, the keys tab | |`outline-editor.js` |In-place editor: temp tiddler, placeholder, save, continue, conflict handling | |`outline-menu.js` |Menus at the selection: block menu (Alt-Enter: insert / convert / edit; from the editor: convert only) and delete confirmation (Delete); keyboard and mouse | |`outline-clipboard.js` |The browser's copy / cut / paste events on the focused outline: the adapter's `copy` gives `{kind, source}`, written as the outline format, as plain text (source) and as HTML (source rendered, tiddler links as text); cut is copy plus `deleteUnit`; paste reads the outline format or plain text (adapter `clipKind`), `paste` parses the clip with the model and rewrites only its item markers / heading levels for the place, one write | |`outline-undo.js` |Undo/redo: every `writeText` records the text before and after plus the selection in `$:/temp/rimir/outline/undo/`; `undoGroup` makes the save and the operation of a split, merge or editor move one step; undo writes only over the text it left | |`language/blocks.multids` |Labels of the block types and menu groups | |`ui/*` |Toolbar button and icon, body template and its filter, help bar (? button and overview), editor template, transclusion marker | |`styles.tid` |Selection frame and item box, compact editor, marker | !! Routing `ui/toolbar-button` toggles `$:/state/rimir/outline/on/<title>` (`yes`/`no`). `ui/body-filter` (a `$:/tags/ViewTemplateBodyFilter` entry) routes eligible tiddlers with state `yes` to `ui/body`, which renders `<$outline>` around the usual block transclusion, plus the ? button and, while `$:/temp/rimir/outline/help/<title>` is `yes`, the key overview. Both sit outside `<$outline>`, so they never become units; the widget only sets and deletes that temp tiddler (`?`, Escape). !! Editor The editor is a real TW edit widget bound to a temp tiddler (`$:/temp/rimir/outline/...`), placed where the unit was. It lives outside the rendered body's widget tree, so a re-render of the body does not destroy it. Typing changes only the temp tiddler; the real tiddler changes once per save. The buffer holds the unit's content only: an item's marker and a heading's `!`s (plus the spaces after them), a code block's or `<<<` quote's fence lines, and the first `>` of each line of a whole quote stay in the tiddler and are not part of the edit (`editSource`/`replace` in the adapter). `ui/editor` renders a compact textarea (no toolbar, SimpleEngine) or, with `$:/config/rimir/outline/full-editor` = `yes`, the full text editor with toolbar. !! Block menu Alt-Enter in selection mode opens `.rr-ol-menu`, absolutely positioned below the selected unit in `.rr-ol`. Its entries: //Insert after// (every block type; not for a single list item) and //Turn into// (the adapter's `convertTypes`). Insert opens a new-unit editor with a `blockType` (kept in the buffer field `outline-block-type`); saving calls the adapter's `insertBlock`, which puts a new heading after the anchor heading's whole section and any other block right after the heading line (`insertsAfterSubtree`; the editor is placed accordingly). Turn into runs `operate("convert", type)`: a bullet switches its marker character with all its siblings of that level (and their sub-items at that marker position), a whole list at all levels; paragraphs, headings and code blocks are rewritten from their content and set apart by blank lines. `convert` parses its result again and refuses it unless the new unit is where the old one was and the unit count changed only by an added list unit. Alt-Enter in the editor (`editMenu`) saves first and opens the menu with the //Turn into// entries only (`openMenu({convertOnly, caret})`); the menu keeps `reedit`, so after the conversion, or on Escape, `editAgain` opens the editor on the unit again with the caret where it was. !! Selection frame Units get the class `rr-ol-selected`. A list item's element contains its sub-items, so for an item with sub-items the frame is an overlay box (`.rr-ol-selbox`, absolutely positioned in `.rr-ol`) around the item's own lines, measured with a DOM range up to the nested list. It is redrawn on every selection change and when the outline container resizes (ResizeObserver). A re-render of an ancestor (for example a changed `$:/tags/Global` or `$:/tags/Macro` tiddler re-renders the page template) or closing the tiddler destroys the `$outline` widget. A buffer that differs from what the editor started with is then kept: it carries `outline-orig-source`, `outline-orig-start`, `outline-orig-text`, `outline-is-new` and `outline-unit-kind`, and the next `$outline` widget of the tiddler reopens the editor at the unit, located as on save (or with the conflict notice when the unit is gone). Escape and switching outline mode off discard it. !! Writes A single `wiki.addTiddler` of the old tiddler plus the new `text` and modification fields. Before writing, the text must equal the text the positions were computed from, otherwise the view re-renders first. If the text is this view's own last write (a key pressed before the refresh after a write), the operation goes on on the rebuilt mapping; after any other change nothing is written. Structural operations pass a model guard (`checkOp` in `model.js`) before they are written: the result is parsed again, and a move must keep the unit count and the kinds and levels; indent/promote must keep the unit count and change only the operated subtree's levels, by exactly one. Anything else is refused without a write. Structural keys do nothing while the view has an open editor. </$fill> </$transclude> "},"$:/plugins/rimir/outline/doc/dev-workflow":{"title":"$:/plugins/rimir/outline/doc/dev-workflow","created":"20261120120000000","modified":"20261120120000000","rdt.hub-category":"tools","rdt.hub-category-name":"Tools","rdt.hub-order":"6","rdt.plugin-key":"outline","rdt.plugin-name":"outline","rdt.plugin-subtitle":"Select, edit, move and indent blocks of a tiddler in place","rdt.order":"3","rdt.section":"Dev Workflow","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"<$transclude $tiddler="$:/plugins/rimir/doc-template/templates/page"> <$fill $name="body"> !! Tests ``` bin/tw test outline # Jasmine, all outline specs bin/tw test # the whole suite ``` Specs live in `test/`: `test-parser-pins.js` (parser positions), `test-model.js`, `test-text-utils.js`, `test-indent.js`, `test-move.js`, `test-edit.js`, `test-editor.js`, `test-keys.js`, `test-widget.js`, with shared fixtures in `fixtures.js`. !! Invariants Every operation test uses one shared assertion: only the unit's range (and the swapped sibling's) changes, a no-op returns the identical string, and an operation followed by its inverse restores the text exactly. !! Adding a format A format adapter registers in `formats.js` and provides `indent`, `promote`, `move`, `replace`, `insertNew`, `remove`, `editSource` and `isMultiline` for one content type. Markdown is planned as the second adapter. !! Restart All JS modules (`module-type: widget` and library modules) need a server restart or reload. Which tiddlers can be outlined? Wikitext tiddlers (`text/vnd.tiddlywiki`) that are not drafts, system tiddlers, `code-body` or `hide-body` tiddlers. v1 is wikitext only; Markdown comes later through a second format adapter. !! Where does the button show? In the view toolbar, per tiddler. State is `$:/state/rimir/outline/on/<title>`. !! How do I put a heading above a list or paragraph? Select the list (or paragraph, or lower heading), Alt-Enter, and pick a heading under //Insert before//. Or insert it anywhere after and press Alt-Up: a heading moves up over the blocks above it. !! Can I move a unit into another list or section? Across heading lines, yes: a paragraph or list at the end of a section moves down into the next section, the first block of a section moves up out of it, and a heading moves up over the blocks above it (they join its section). List items stay in their list and blocks stay in their HTML container. To take a unit anywhere else, into another list, section or tiddler: Ctrl-X, select the place, Ctrl-V; the paste adapts its levels. !! Can I paste a copied unit into an e-mail? Yes. Ctrl-C on a selected unit puts it on the system clipboard as HTML (rendered: lists, headings, tables, code; TiddlyWiki's styles do not come along, links to tiddlers become plain text) and as its wikitext. E-mail, Jira and other rich text editors paste the HTML, plain text fields the wikitext. Pasted back into an outline, also in another wiki, the levels adapt to the place. !! Are widgets and macros editable inside? No. `<$list>`, `<$reveal>`, macro and procedure calls are single units: select, move or edit their source as a whole. Only plain HTML containers are opened. !! Plugins that replace core widgets (copy buttons on code blocks, ...)? A plugin can replace a core widget with its own `\widget` definition, for example `$codeblock` (kookma's utility plugin adds a caption and a copy button). The replacement renders without source positions; outline assigns it to the next unit of that type in document order, and frames, edits and moves it like any other block. What it renders inside stays untouched. !! Why can't I select a block? Units that render nothing (for example a procedure call with empty output) have no DOM node and cannot be selected. !! What happens when I save an empty unit? A unit without children is deleted. A unit with children is not: the save is refused with a notice. A new unit (from Enter) that stays empty writes nothing. !! What if the tiddler changes while I edit? Your text is kept. On save the unit is looked up again by its original source: if it occurs exactly once, the save goes there; otherwise the editor stays open with a notice. !! Two views of the same tiddler? Only one view can edit at a time. !! What happens to an unsaved edit? Escape or toggling outline mode off discards it. If you changed the text and the view is rendered again (for example after a global macro changed) or you close the tiddler, the text is kept: the editor opens again at the unit as soon as the tiddler is shown in outline mode. If the unit is gone by then, the editor opens with the "changed underneath" notice, so you can copy your text. Kept text lives in a `$:/temp/` tiddler and is gone after a reload. !! Why does Alt-Up/Down add a blank line? When a list, code block or table is followed directly (single line break) by a paragraph, swapping them as they are would merge the paragraph with its new neighbour. Such blocks get a blank line between them. Items and headings keep their line breaks. A comment (or other text that is not a unit) between the two blocks is kept and set apart by blank lines too. !! Why does Alt-Up/Down sometimes do nothing? A move swaps a unit with its neighbour inside the same parent (an item only with an item of the same level, a heading with a heading of the same level) or moves it across one heading line (see the reference); at the first or last place there is nothing to move over. Before writing, outline re-parses the result; if the swap would change the units (for example a heading section whose last paragraph would merge with the next block), the move is refused and the text stays unchanged. Add a blank line between the blocks by hand and try again. !! Do Tab and Alt-Up/Down work while I edit? Yes. They save your text, indent, promote or move the unit with its subtree, and keep editing it at its new place with the cursor where it was. With empty text they do nothing. !! My CSS for `.tc-tiddler-body > p` stopped working While outline mode is on, the body is wrapped in `div.rr-ol`, so child selectors of `.tc-tiddler-body` no longer match. Use a descendant selector (`.tc-tiddler-body p`) or also match `.tc-tiddler-body > .rr-ol > p`. !! Do `AI:` lines of llm-inline fire? No. Outline writes bypass `th-saving-tiddler`, which llm-inline listens to. `AI:` lines typed in outline mode do not fire; they do after a normal editor save. !! Why doesn't the editor show the `*` or `!`? The editor edits a unit's content. The list marker and the heading level are structure: change them with Tab/Shift-Tab. If you type the item's own marker at the start anyway (for example `* ` in a `*` item), it is dropped instead of doubled. !! How do I put a line break into a bullet? Shift-Enter in the editor. In wikitext a list item (and a heading) is one source line, and a real line break would end it: the next line would become a paragraph that swallows the following items. So line breaks in items and headings are saved as `<br>`, and an existing `<br>` shows as a line break when you edit. Enter stays //save and new item//. Paragraphs and other blocks keep real line breaks. !! Why does switching one bullet to numbered switch its neighbours too? In wikitext the list type is the marker character, and items of one level with different characters do not form one list: one numbered item among bullets would cut the list into three. So //Turn into// switches all items of that level under the same parent; their sub-items keep their own type. !! Do editor plugins work? Yes, the editor is TW's own edit widget. AutoComplete handles Enter, Escape, Tab and the arrows first; outline keys act only if the event was not consumed. !! Does Tab leave the page? No, while a unit is selected Tab is used for indent. </$fill> </$transclude> "},"$:/plugins/rimir/outline/doc/overview":{"title":"$:/plugins/rimir/outline/doc/overview","created":"20261120120000000","modified":"20261120120000000","rdt.hub-category":"tools","rdt.hub-category-name":"Tools","rdt.hub-order":"6","rdt.plugin-key":"outline","rdt.plugin-name":"outline","rdt.plugin-subtitle":"Select, edit, move and indent blocks of a tiddler in place","rdt.order":"1","rdt.section":"Overview","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"<$transclude $tiddler="$:/plugins/rimir/doc-template/templates/page"> <$fill $name="body"> !! What it does Outline mode brings the Streams workflow to a normal tiddler. Switch it on for a tiddler with the //outline// button in the view toolbar. The tiddler renders as before; every block that comes from its own text becomes selectable. Select a block, edit it in place, move it, indent it. Each action rewrites the right part of that one tiddler's text. !! How you use it # Press //outline// in the view toolbar (the button is shown for wikitext tiddlers only, not for drafts, system tiddlers, `code-body` or `hide-body` tiddlers). # Click a block or press Up/Down (Left/Right: parent / first child). A whole list counts as one block for Up/Down; Right enters it, Ctrl-Up/Down step through every item. A blue frame marks the selected unit. A small badge in the right margin names each unit's type (paragraph, h2, code-block, bullet, ...), so heading levels and block types are easy to tell apart; the editor field carries the badge of what it edits. The settings switch it to headings only or off. On a list item it frames only the item's own line; moves still take its sub-items along. # Alt-Up/Alt-Down move it (also across heading lines), Tab/Shift-Tab indent or promote it. Its subtree goes along. Alt-Enter inserts a block after or before it, Ctrl-Enter starts a new empty unit below it; an empty tiddler starts with Enter. # Enter (or a double-click) opens the editor in place, the caret at the end of the text: a compact one-line field (the full editor with toolbar is a setting). It shows the content only, without the list marker or heading `!`s, a code block's fence lines or the `>`s of a quote, so editing never changes the nesting. Ctrl-Enter saves, Enter saves and opens a new unit (at the start of a filled item or paragraph: an empty one above), Escape discards. Ctrl-Up/Down save and move the editor to the previous/next unit, Alt-Enter turns it into another type. # Delete removes the selected unit with everything below it, after a yes/no menu; on a heading the menu also offers to delete just the heading line. In the editor, Enter in the middle of a list item splits it at the caret, Backspace at its start merges it into the item above and Delete at its end pulls the item below up. Ctrl-Z undoes any of these changes, Ctrl-Y redoes, in the editor too while nothing is typed. Ctrl-C / Ctrl-X / Ctrl-V copy, cut and paste a unit with its subtree through the system clipboard: formatted into an e-mail, or into another tiddler, where a paste takes the level of the place. # Alt-Enter opens the block menu: insert a new block of a type after or before the selection, or turn the selection into another type; in the editor it turns the edited unit into another type. # On a transclusion line, Enter opens the target tiddler, already in outline mode. # `?` (or the small ? button at the top right) shows all keys next to the outline; Escape closes it. The //keys// tab has the same overview, the settings tab changes the keys. !! Units * List items (`*`, `#`, `;`, `:`, `>`) - the item's own lines; nested items are its subtree. * Lists as a whole. * Headings, with their section (up to the next heading of the same or a higher level) as subtree. * Paragraphs, code blocks, tables. * Plain HTML containers (`<div>`, `<section>`, ...) are opened: their inner blocks are units, and the container is one too. * Transclusion lines (`{{...}}`, `<$transclude/>`). * Widgets (`<$list>`, `<$reveal>`, ...) and macro or procedure calls: opaque, one unit each. Pragmas (`\define`, `\procedure`, `\import`, ...) are never units. A unit that renders nothing cannot be selected. !! Read-only wikis With `$:/status/IsReadOnly` = yes, only navigation (selection, transclusion jump) works. </$fill> </$transclude> "},"$:/plugins/rimir/outline/doc/reference":{"title":"$:/plugins/rimir/outline/doc/reference","created":"20261120120000000","modified":"20261120120000000","rdt.hub-category":"tools","rdt.hub-category-name":"Tools","rdt.hub-order":"6","rdt.plugin-key":"outline","rdt.plugin-name":"outline","rdt.plugin-subtitle":"Select, edit, move and indent blocks of a tiddler in place","rdt.order":"6","rdt.section":"Reference","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"<$transclude $tiddler="$:/plugins/rimir/doc-template/templates/page"> <$fill $name="body"> !! Keys |!Shortcut tiddler |!Default |!Action | |`outline-up` / `outline-down` |Up / Down |Select previous / next unit. A whole list counts as one block: Down from a selected list goes to the block after it, Up from below a list selects the whole list; inside a list they go item by item | |`outline-up-deep` / `outline-down-deep` |ctrl-Up / ctrl-Down |Select previous / next unit in document order, also into lists (from below a list: its last item) | |`outline-parent` / `outline-child` |Left / Right |Select the parent unit (item of a sub-item, whole list of a top-level item, heading of a section) / the first child | |`outline-move-up` / `outline-move-down` |alt-Up / alt-Down |Swap with previous / next sibling | |`outline-indent` / `outline-promote` |Tab / shift-Tab |Demote / promote by one level | |`outline-edit` |Enter |Edit in place (on a transclusion Enter opens the target) | |`outline-add` |ctrl-Enter |Edit a new empty unit below the selected one (see New unit) | |`outline-delete` |Delete |Delete the unit with its subtree, after a confirmation menu (see Delete) | |`outline-undo` / `outline-redo` |ctrl-Z / ctrl-Y, ctrl-shift-Z |Undo / redo the last change made in the outline (see Undo) | |`outline-menu` |alt-Enter |Block menu: insert a new block after or before the unit, or turn it into another type; Up/Down, Enter runs, Escape closes. In the editor: save, then only //Turn into//; the editor opens again on the unit, also after Escape | |`outline-open` |Enter |Open the transclusion target in outline mode | |`outline-clear` |Escape |Clear selection | |`outline-save` |ctrl-Enter |Save the edit | |`outline-continue` |Enter |Save and open a new unit (single-line units). In the middle of a list item's text: split it (see Split); at the start of a filled list item or paragraph: a new empty one above (see New unit) | |`outline-newline` |shift-Enter |Newline in the editor (saved as `<br>` in list items and headings) | |`outline-indent` / `outline-promote` |Tab / shift-Tab |In the editor too: save, indent / promote, keep editing. On an empty new list item: its level (see New unit) | |`outline-move-up` / `outline-move-down` |alt-Up / alt-Down |In the editor too: save, move, keep editing | |`outline-edit-up` |ctrl-Up |Editor only: save and edit the previous unit | |`outline-edit-down` |ctrl-Down |Editor only: save and edit the next unit | |`outline-merge` |Backspace |Editor, caret at the start of a list item: merge it into the item above (see Merge) | |`outline-merge-next` |Delete |Editor, caret at the end of a list item: pull the item below up into it (see Merge) | |`outline-cancel` |Escape |Discard the edit | |`outline-help` |shift-slash |Show / hide the key overview. `?` always works too, whatever the keyboard layout; Escape closes it | All are `$:/config/shortcuts/<name>`; descriptions are in `$:/config/ShortcutInfo/<name>`. Change them in the settings tab (the core shortcut editor, press the key to record it, platform variants included) or in ControlPanel > Keyboard Shortcuts. Copy, cut and paste (Ctrl-C / Ctrl-X / Ctrl-V, Cmd on Mac) are the browser's own keys, not shortcut tiddlers (see Clipboard). !! Type badges |!`data-ol-type` |!Unit | |`paragraph`, `code-block`, `table`, `quote`, `rule` |Blocks (`p`, `pre`, `table`, `blockquote`, `hr`; other blocks: their tag name) | |`h1` … `h6` |Headings | |`bullet`, `numbered`, `term`, `definition`, `quote` |List items (by their list: `ul`, `ol`, `dt`/`dd`, `blockquote`) | |`bullet-list`, `numbered-list`, `definitions`, `quote` |Whole lists (badge in the left margin) | |`transclusion`, `widget` |Transclusion lines, widgets and macro calls | |tag name (`div`, ...) |Opened HTML containers (badge in the left margin) | The widget sets `data-ol-type` on each unit's first DOM node (`unitType` in `dom-utils.js`); CSS shows it as `::after`, absolutely positioned, so the layout does not change. The editor field gets the type of the unit it edits, of the chosen block type, or of its anchor (a new item); an item edited inside its `li` keeps the `li`'s badge. !! Key overview The //keys// tab and the overlay (`?` in an outline, or the small ? button at its top right) show the same table, `$:/plugins/rimir/outline/ui/keys-table`, with the keys read live from the config. Its groups are the tiddlers listed in `$:/plugins/rimir/outline/key-groups`: each has a `caption`, an optional `hint`, a `list` of shortcut names and, optionally, text shown after the keys (the fixed block menu keys). The settings tab uses the same groups. A double-click on a unit opens the editor on it (on a transclusion: its line; links and buttons keep their click). In multi-line units (code blocks, tables, widgets, `"""` items) Enter is a plain newline and only Ctrl-Enter saves. !! Indent and promote * Lists: a list item and its subtree lines get one more of the item's last marker character (`#b` becomes `##b`, `*b` `**b`, `#*` `#**`). No previous sibling: no-op. Promote removes one marker character; depth 1 is a no-op. * Headings: one `!` more on the heading and every heading in its section; no-op if one would pass 6. Promote removes one; level 1 is a no-op. * Other units: Tab and Shift-Tab do nothing. !! Move Swap the unit's whole subtree with the adjacent sibling's whole subtree, blank-line separators preserved. Blocks other than items and headings that touch (a single line break) get a blank line between them and before the following content, so a paragraph cannot absorb its neighbour. First/last child: no-op. * List item: siblings are items of the same list at the same depth. * Heading: siblings are headings of the same level in the same parent. * Other blocks: siblings are blocks in the same section (or HTML container, or root) before any sub-heading. Across heading lines (blocks of a section, never out of an HTML container): * A heading moves up over the block or deeper heading above it: its line goes above that block, which joins its section (`para`, `! New` → `! New`, `para`). * A heading moves down over a following higher heading: its section goes below that heading's line and becomes a sub-section (`!! B`, `y`, `! A` → `! A`, `!! B`, `y`). * A block (paragraph, list, ...) at the end of a section moves down over the next heading line into that section; as the first block of a section it moves up over the heading line out of it. The two are each other's inverse. A heading moving down over a heading of the same level swaps the two sections, as before; one with blocks under it does not move down over them (use Alt-Up on the block, or on the next heading). !! Delete The unit goes with its subtree: an item with its sub-items, a heading with its section, a list with its items, a container with its contents. An only item takes its list along and an only child its container (neither can stay empty). Separators as for a blank save: one blank line stays between the neighbours. The selection goes to the unit that now starts there. |!Selected |!Menu | |Heading with a section |Yes, the heading and its section (N blocks) · Just the heading (its section joins the one above) · Cancel | |Whole list / item with sub-items / container |Yes, ... (N items / sub-items / blocks) · Cancel | |Anything else |Yes, delete · Cancel | The first entry is active: Delete, Enter deletes; Escape cancels. List items without sub-items are deleted at once while `$:/config/rimir/outline/quick-delete-items` is `yes` (the default); `no` asks for them too. The model guard refuses a result that removes other units than these (e.g. two lists that would merge). !! Undo In selection mode Ctrl-Z takes back the last change made in the outline: a move, indent, delete, merge, split, conversion or saved edit; Ctrl-Y (or Ctrl-Shift-Z) does it again. The selection goes back to where it was before the change. A split or merge, and Tab / Alt-Up/Down while editing, save the edited text and change the structure in one step. Inside the editor Ctrl-Z and Ctrl-Y are the outline's undo and redo while the field still has the text it opened with (nothing typed, or the typing undone): so a split, merge or move made from the editor is taken back at once, and the editor opens again on the unit selected afterwards. With typed text they are the text field's own. The history is kept per tiddler in `$:/temp/rimir/outline/undo/<title>` for the running session only, the last `$:/config/rimir/outline/undo-depth` steps (default 20). A new change empties the redo steps. Undo writes only while the tiddler still has the text the outline left: when it was changed elsewhere (another editor, a sync), the history is dropped and nothing is written. Read-only wikis: nothing. !! Clipboard In selection mode Ctrl-C copies the selected unit with its subtree (an item with its sub-items, a heading with its section, a whole list, a container with its contents) to the system clipboard, Ctrl-X cuts it: the same, then it is deleted without the Delete menu (Ctrl-Z brings it back). Ctrl-V pastes after the selected unit and selects what it pasted; in a tiddler without units it goes at the end. These are the browser's own copy, cut and paste (Cmd on Mac, the Edit menu works too), so the keys cannot be changed in the shortcut settings. A copied unit flashes briefly. In the editor, and while text is marked with the mouse, they act on text as usual; read-only wikis: copy only. A copy puts three formats on the clipboard: |!Format |!Content |!Used by | |`text/html` |the unit rendered (its wikitext source rendered in this tiddler's context), without CSS classes; links to tiddlers become their text |e-mail, Jira and other rich text editors | |`text/plain` |the wikitext source |text fields, a TiddlyWiki editor | |`application/x-rimir-outline` |JSON `{kind, source}` (kind `items`, `heading` or `block`) |a paste into an outline, also in another tab or wiki | In the HTML and the plain text, copied list items start at level 1 (a sub-item copied alone has no empty bullets above it); the outline format keeps the source as it is. A paste takes the outline format when it is there, else the plain text as wikitext: one list is pasted as items, one heading with its section as a heading, anything else as it is. HTML from elsewhere is not converted, only its plain text is used. The levels adapt to the place (only real list markers and heading `!`s change, not lines inside a code block): |!Copied \ selected |!List item |!Whole list |!Heading |!Other block | |Items |after the item's sub-items, at its level; sub-items keep their extra marker characters (`* a`, `** a1` after `## y` → `## a`, `##* a1`) |at the end of the list, at its top level |a new list right below the heading line |a new list after the block | |Heading |after the outermost list |after the list |after the heading's section, at its level |after the block | |Block |after the outermost list |after the list |right below the heading line |after the block | A new list starts at level 1 (`#* a`, `#** b` → `* a`, `** b`). A heading after anything but a heading gets one level below the heading of the section it lands in (level 1 outside any section); its sub-headings keep their distance, at most level 6. Blocks are set apart by blank lines. !! Merge (Backspace) In the editor, caret at the very start of a list item (nothing selected): the item's text goes to the end of the item above it in the list (the previous item in document order: the parent, or the last sub-item of the previous sibling), the item's line goes, its sub-items keep their lines and levels. The editor continues in the item above, at the join. An empty item is simply deleted (also one with sub-items) and the editor goes to the end of the item above; an empty new item is discarded the same way. The first item of a list, other units and multi-line items: a normal Backspace. Delete with the caret at the very end of a list item is the same merge from above: the item below that Backspace would merge into this one (the next item in document order: the first sub-item, or the next item of the list) comes up, the caret stays at the join. The last item of a list, blank, new and multi-line items: a normal Delete. !! Split (Enter) In the editor, caret inside a list item's text (not at its start or end, nothing selected): the text before the caret stays in the item, the text after it goes to a new item directly below, which is edited with the caret at its start. The new item is a sibling with the same marker; when the item has sub-items it becomes their first one, so the sub-items stay with the item. Backspace at the new item's start (merge) gives back the original line. !! Empty tiddler A tiddler without units (empty, or only whitespace and comments) shows a hint. Enter (or Ctrl-Enter) opens the editor for a first paragraph, Alt-Enter the block menu with the insert types only; the block goes at the end of the text. !! New unit (Enter) Enter at the end of the editor saves and opens a new unit after the edited one; Ctrl-Enter in selection mode opens the same new unit after the selected one, without editing that first: * List item (also a quote line): same marker, after the item's whole subtree. While it is still empty, Tab / Shift-Tab set its level (one marker character more / less; at most one level below the item above it, at least level 1); the field moves with it and it is written with that marker. * Heading: paragraph directly under the heading line. * Paragraph, and anything else (code block, table, whole list, ...): paragraph after it. Enter with the caret at the very start of a filled list item or paragraph saves the edited text and opens an empty new unit right above it: an item with the same marker (sub-items stay with the item below), or a paragraph. Escape or an empty save leaves the text as it was. !! Block menu Insert before offers the same types as Insert after and puts the block directly above the selected unit (it ends the section above; above a list or a lower heading this is the way to put a heading in front of it). Turning a paragraph or heading into a bulleted or numbered item next to a list of that type joins that list (TW continues a list over blank lines). |!Selected |!Insert after / before |!Turn into | |Paragraph |Paragraph, Heading 1–3, Bulleted/Numbered list, Quote, Code block |Heading 1–3, Bulleted/Numbered list, Quote, Code block | |Heading |the same (a heading goes after the section, other blocks right below the heading) |Paragraph, Bulleted/Numbered list, Quote, Code block | |Code block |the same |Paragraph, Bulleted/Numbered list, Quote | |Whole list |the same |Bulleted ↔ Numbered (all levels) | |List item |– |Bulleted ↔ Numbered (with all its siblings of that level) | |Transclusion |the same, plus //Edit this line// first |– | !! State and config |!Tiddler |!Purpose | |`$:/state/rimir/outline/on/<title>` |Outline mode on (`yes`) / off | |`$:/temp/rimir/outline/...` |Editor buffer, selection, open key overview (`help/<title>`), undo history (`undo/<title>`, JSON) while active | |`$:/config/rimir/outline/badges` |Type badges: `all` (default), `headings` (h1–h6 only) or `off`. Sets class `rr-ol-badges-<mode>` on the frame; the badge text is the unit's `data-ol-type` | |`$:/config/rimir/outline/quick-delete-items` |`yes` (default): Delete removes list items without sub-items without asking; `no`: always ask | |`$:/config/rimir/outline/undo-depth` |Number of undo steps kept per tiddler (default 20) | |`$:/config/rimir/outline/full-editor` |`yes`: full text editor with toolbar; otherwise (default `no`) the compact one-line editor | </$fill> </$transclude> "},"$:/plugins/rimir/outline/doc/tw-internals":{"title":"$:/plugins/rimir/outline/doc/tw-internals","created":"20261120120000000","modified":"20261120120000000","rdt.hub-category":"tools","rdt.hub-category-name":"Tools","rdt.hub-order":"6","rdt.plugin-key":"outline","rdt.plugin-name":"outline","rdt.plugin-subtitle":"Select, edit, move and indent blocks of a tiddler in place","rdt.order":"7","rdt.section":"TW Internals","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"<$transclude $tiddler="$:/plugins/rimir/doc-template/templates/page"> <$fill $name="body"> !! Parser positions The plugin relies on the wikitext parser's source offsets. `WikiParser.parseBlock` sets `start`, `end` and `rule` on every top-level block node. The list rule sets them on each list item: from the marker to the end of the item's own line, nested child lines excluded. Every widget keeps its parse node as `widget.parseTreeNode`, so a widget tree walk recovers the ranges. Units are recomputed after every render and are valid only for the text they were computed from. !! `{{X}}` is a "tiddler" node A block transclusion `{{X}}` parses to a node of type `tiddler`, not `transclude`; the walker maps it to the transclusion unit. Widgets rendered from a transcluded tiddler carry offsets into //that// tiddler's text, so descent stops at a transclude to another tiddler. !! Widget mapping rule A unit's DOM node is found by matching the parse node's `start` and tag; `end` is the tie-breaker when several widgets share a start (for example a list and its first item). !! Pragmas and typed blocks A pragma such as `\define` parses to a `set` node that wraps the rest of the tree; the walker steps through it, and the pragma itself is never a unit. For `$$$` typed blocks the parser starts the node at the line after the `$$$` header, so the widget match uses that line as the unit's anchor instead of the unit start (see `outline-widget.js`). !! Pin tests `test/test-parser-pins.js` pins the offsets for list items, a heading and a paragraph, a block transclusion (`{{X}}` parses to a `tiddler` node), pragma wrapping (`\define` yields a `set` node that wraps the following blocks), a code block, a table and a block-mode HTML container. Widgets are not pinned. A TW update that changes them fails the suite loudly. !! Why writes bypass `th-saving-tiddler` A write is `wiki.addTiddler` of the old tiddler with new `text` plus `getModificationFields()`. It is not an editor save, and a single splice per action must not trigger editor-save hooks. Consequence: listeners on `th-saving-tiddler`, such as llm-inline's `AI:` lines, do not fire. !! Editor and AutoComplete AutoComplete listens on `document` in the capture phase, so its handler runs before the outline key handler, which checks `event.defaultPrevented`. </$fill> </$transclude> "},"$:/plugins/rimir/outline/documentation":{"title":"$:/plugins/rimir/outline/documentation","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"<$list filter="[[$:/plugins/rimir/doc-template]plugin-type[plugin]]" variable="ignore"> {{$:/plugins/rimir/outline/doc/overview||$:/plugins/rimir/doc-template/doc-viewer}} </$list> <$list filter="[[$:/plugins/rimir/doc-template]plugin-type[plugin]!match[plugin]]" variable="ignore"> <div class="rr-settings-info-card"> ''doc-template'' plugin is not installed. See the <<tag readme>> tab for documentation. </div> </$list> "},"$:/plugins/rimir/outline/dom-utils.js":{"title":"$:/plugins/rimir/outline/dom-utils.js","text":"/*\ title: $:/plugins/rimir/outline/dom-utils.js type: application/javascript module-type: library DOM helpers shared by outline-keys.js and outline-editor.js. They work on the browser DOM and on TW's fake DOM (no nextSibling/contains there; removeChild keeps parentNode). \*/ "use strict"; exports.setClass = function(node, cls, on) { var list = (node.className || "").split(" ").filter(function(c) { return c && c !== cls; }); if(on) { list.push(cls); } if(list.length) { node.className = list.join(" "); } else if(node.removeAttribute) { node.removeAttribute("class"); } }; exports.focus = function(node) { if(node && node.focus) { node.focus({preventScroll: true}); } }; /* The first of a unit's DOM nodes that takes up space on the page (has layout boxes), else the first one. Plugins can put hidden elements in front of a unit's own (an empty, hidden caption before a code block): menus and scrolling go by what is shown. */ exports.firstShown = function(nodes) { for(var i = 0; i < nodes.length; i++) { if(nodes[i].getClientRects && nodes[i].getClientRects().length) { return nodes[i]; } } return nodes[0]; }; exports.scrollIntoView = function(node) { if(node && node.scrollIntoView) { node.scrollIntoView({block: "nearest"}); } }; // True for input/textarea/select and contenteditable elements and their descendants exports.isEditable = function(node) { for(; node && node.nodeType === 1; node = node.parentNode) { var tag = (node.tagName || "").toLowerCase(); if(tag === "input" || tag === "textarea" || tag === "select" || node.isContentEditable) { return true; } } return false; }; exports.nextSiblingOf = function(node) { if(node.nextSibling !== undefined) { return node.nextSibling; } var siblings = node.parentNode ? node.parentNode.childNodes : [], i = siblings.indexOf(node); return i === -1 ? null : (siblings[i + 1] || null); }; exports.firstChildOf = function(node) { return node.firstChild || null; }; // True when `node` is attached below (or is) `ancestor` exports.isInside = function(node, ancestor) { if(!node || !ancestor) { return false; } if(ancestor.contains) { return ancestor.contains(node); } while(node && node !== ancestor) { var parent = node.parentNode; if(!parent || parent.childNodes.indexOf(node) === -1) { return false; } node = parent; } return node === ancestor; }; function tagOf(node) { return node ? String(node.tagName || node.tag || "").toLowerCase() : ""; } var LIST_TYPES = {ul: "bullet-list", ol: "numbered-list", dl: "definitions", blockquote: "quote"}, ITEM_TYPES = {ul: "bullet", ol: "numbered", blockquote: "quote"}, BLOCK_TYPES = {p: "paragraph", pre: "code-block", table: "table", blockquote: "quote", hr: "rule"}, // Types of the block menu (format-wikitext BLOCK_TYPES) as badge types NEW_BLOCK_TYPES = {paragraph: "paragraph", heading1: "h1", heading2: "h2", heading3: "h3", bulleted: "bullet", numbered: "numbered", quote: "quote", code: "code-block"}; /* Badge type of a unit (kind) from its first DOM node: paragraph, h1-h6, code-block, table, quote, rule, bullet, numbered, term, definition, bullet-list, numbered-list, definitions, transclusion, widget, or the tag name. Shown by CSS (attr(data-ol-type)) when badges are on. */ exports.unitType = function(kind, node) { var tag = tagOf(node); switch(kind) { case "heading": return /^h[1-6]$/.test(tag) ? tag : "heading"; case "item": return tag === "dt" ? "term" : tag === "dd" ? "definition" : ITEM_TYPES[tagOf(node.parentNode)] || "item"; case "list": return LIST_TYPES[tag] || "list"; case "block": return BLOCK_TYPES[tag] || tag || "block"; case "transclusion": return "transclusion"; case "widget": return "widget"; default: return tag || kind; } }; exports.newBlockType = function(blockType) { return NEW_BLOCK_TYPES[blockType] || ""; }; ","type":"application/javascript","module-type":"library"},"$:/plugins/rimir/outline/format-wikitext.js":{"title":"$:/plugins/rimir/outline/format-wikitext.js","text":"/*\ title: $:/plugins/rimir/outline/format-wikitext.js type: application/javascript module-type: outline-format Wikitext adapter: indent, promote, move, replace, insertNew, remove, deleteUnit, merge, split, copy, paste. Functions take (text, model, id) and return null or {text, select}. \*/ "use strict"; var utils = require("$:/plugins/rimir/outline/text-utils.js"), outlineModel = require("$:/plugins/rimir/outline/model.js"); exports.types = ["text/vnd.tiddlywiki", ""]; // A separator that contains an empty line var BLANK_LINE = /\n[ \t]*\r?\n/; // Units of `kind` whose start lies in the subtree of u (u included) function subtreeUnits(model, u, kind) { return model.units.filter(function(d) { return d.kind === kind && d.start >= u.start && d.start < u.subtreeEnd; }); } // positions: [{pos, insert}] / removals; applied from the end backwards function apply(text, edits) { edits.sort(function(a, b) { return b.pos - a.pos; }); edits.forEach(function(e) { text = utils.splice(text, e.pos, e.pos + e.remove, e.insert); }); return text; } function selectFor(u, edits) { // units start never moves: edits at u.start insert before it only for headings, where start stays return u.start; } exports.indent = function(text, model, id) { var u = model.units[id], edits; if(!u) { return null; } if(u.kind === "item") { var sibs = u.parent === -1 ? model.roots : model.units[u.parent].children, i = sibs.indexOf(id); if(i < 1 || model.units[sibs[i - 1]].kind !== "item") { return null; } var c = u.marker.charAt(u.level - 1); edits = subtreeUnits(model, u, "item").map(function(d) { return {pos: d.start + u.level, remove: 0, insert: c}; }); } else if(u.kind === "heading") { var hs = subtreeUnits(model, u, "heading"); if(hs.some(function(h) { return h.level >= 6; })) { return null; } edits = hs.map(function(h) { return {pos: h.start, remove: 0, insert: "!"}; }); } else { return null; } return {text: apply(text, edits), select: selectFor(u, edits)}; }; exports.promote = function(text, model, id) { var u = model.units[id], edits; if(!u) { return null; } if(u.kind === "item") { if(u.level <= 1) { return null; } edits = subtreeUnits(model, u, "item").map(function(d) { return {pos: d.start + u.level - 1, remove: 1, insert: ""}; }); } else if(u.kind === "heading") { if(u.level <= 1) { return null; } edits = subtreeUnits(model, u, "heading").map(function(h) { return {pos: h.start, remove: 1, insert: ""}; }); } else { return null; } return {text: apply(text, edits), select: selectFor(u, edits)}; }; /* Swap the unit's whole subtree with the adjacent sibling of the same class (heading vs non-heading). Items and headings keep the separators as they are. Other blocks that touch (single line break) get a blank line between them and before the content after the pair, because after the swap a paragraph would otherwise absorb the block after it. Non-whitespace between the blocks (a comment) is kept and set apart by blank lines. */ /* Alt-Up/Down. Siblings swap with their subtrees: items and headings only with one of the same kind and level, other blocks with other blocks. Across a heading line ("cross", block level only, not out of a container): - a heading moves up over the block or deeper heading above it (its line goes above, that block joins its section); - a heading moves down over a following higher heading (its section goes below that line and becomes a sub-section); - a block moves down over the next heading line (into that section) and up over its section's heading line. Whole blocks are set apart by blank lines. The result has the moved unit's new start (select) and cross: true for a move across a heading line. */ exports.move = function(text, model, id, dir) { var u = model.units[id]; if(!u || (dir !== -1 && dir !== 1)) { return null; } var sibs = u.parent === -1 ? model.roots : model.units[u.parent].children, i = sibs.indexOf(id), o = model.units[sibs[i + dir]]; if(i < 0) { return null; } if(u.kind === "item") { if(!o || o.kind !== "item" || o.level !== u.level) { return null; } return swap(text, o, u, dir, false); } if(u.kind === "heading") { if(o && o.kind === "heading" && o.level === u.level) { return swap(text, o, u, dir, false); } if(dir < 0 && o && (o.kind !== "heading" || o.level > u.level)) { return swapRanges(text, o.start, o.subtreeEnd, u.start, u.end, o.start, true); } if(dir > 0 && o && o.kind === "heading" && o.level < u.level) { return swapRanges(text, u.start, u.subtreeEnd, o.start, o.end, -1, true); } return null; } if(o && o.kind !== "heading") { return swap(text, o, u, dir, true); } if(dir > 0) { var h = o || nextHeading(model, u); return h ? swapRanges(text, u.start, u.subtreeEnd, h.start, h.end, -1, true) : null; } var p = !o && u.parent !== -1 ? model.units[u.parent] : null; return p && p.kind === "heading" ? swapRanges(text, p.start, p.end, u.start, u.subtreeEnd, p.start, true) : null; }; // Swap sibling u with its neighbour o (dir -1: o is above) with their subtrees function swap(text, o, u, dir, blocks) { var a = dir < 0 ? o : u, b = dir < 0 ? u : o, r = swapRanges(text, a.start, a.subtreeEnd, b.start, b.subtreeEnd, dir < 0 ? a.start : -1, blocks); delete r.cross; return r; } /* Swap range A [a0, a1) with the later range B [b0, b1): A's text goes where B was and vice versa. `select`: the moved unit's new start, -1 when it is A's text (it then starts after B's text and the separator). `blocks`: set the two apart, and the text after them, by blank lines (anything between them, e.g. a comment, stays between them). */ function swapRanges(text, a0, a1, b0, b1, select, blocks) { var A = text.substring(a0, a1), sep = text.substring(a1, b0), B = text.substring(b0, b1), rest = text.substring(b1); if(blocks) { var nl = utils.eol(text), gap = /^(?:[ \t]*\r?\n)*/.exec(rest)[0]; if(/\S/.test(sep)) { // Keep anything between the blocks (e.g. a comment), set apart by blank lines on both sides sep = nl + nl + sep.trim() + nl + nl; } else if(!BLANK_LINE.test(sep)) { sep = nl + nl; } // Only whole line breaks are normalised, so the next line keeps its indentation if(/\S/.test(rest) && !BLANK_LINE.test(gap)) { rest = nl + nl + rest.substring(gap.length); } } return { text: text.substring(0, a0) + B + sep + A + rest, select: select === -1 ? a0 + B.length + sep.length : select, cross: true }; } // The heading that starts right after block u in document order, in the same container (or at the root); or null function nextHeading(model, u) { var next = null; model.units.forEach(function(x) { if(x.start >= u.subtreeEnd && (!next || x.start < next.start)) { next = x; } }); return next && next.kind === "heading" && sectionRoot(model, next) === sectionRoot(model, u) ? next : null; } // The nearest ancestor of u that is not a heading (a container), or -1 function sectionRoot(model, u) { var p = u.parent; while(p !== -1 && model.units[p].kind === "heading") { p = model.units[p].parent; } return p; } // Replace the unit's own source with newSource /* Offset where the unit's content starts: after an item's marker or a heading's "!"s and the spaces after them. The editor shows and replaces only the content, so it cannot change the nesting. */ function contentStart(text, u) { var prefix = u.kind === "item" ? u.marker : u.kind === "heading" ? new Array(u.level + 1).join("!") : ""; if(!prefix || text.substring(u.start, u.start + prefix.length) !== prefix) { return u.start; } var pos = u.start + prefix.length; return pos + /^[ \t]*/.exec(text.substring(pos, u.end))[0].length; } // Text typed with the unit's own marker and a space in front (out of habit) loses that marker function stripTypedMarker(u, source) { if(u.kind === "item" && source && source.substring(0, u.marker.length) === u.marker && /^[ \t]/.test(source.substring(u.marker.length))) { return source.substring(u.marker.length).replace(/^[ \t]+/, ""); } return source; } /* Items and headings are one source line: a real line break would end the item (the next line becomes a paragraph that swallows the following items). Their line breaks are stored as <br>; the editor shows them as line breaks. */ function isOneLine(u) { return u.kind === "item" || u.kind === "heading"; } function toBreaks(source) { return source.replace(/^(?:[ \t]*\r?\n)+|(?:\r?\n[ \t]*)+$/g, "").replace(/[ \t]*\r?\n/g, "<br>"); } /* Fence lines of a code block (```lang ... ```) or a <<< quote block (<<<class ... <<< citation) that the editor leaves out: {open, content, close} (content lines joined by \n), or null for other units. */ function fenced(text, u) { var fence = u.tag === "codeblock" ? /^```/ : (u.kind === "block" && u.tag === "blockquote" ? /^<<</ : null), lines = fence ? text.substring(u.start, u.end).split(/\r?\n/) : []; if(lines.length < 2 || !fence.test(lines[0]) || !fence.test(lines[lines.length - 1])) { return null; } return {open: lines[0], content: lines.slice(1, -1).join("\n"), close: lines[lines.length - 1]}; } // A whole quote of > lines: the editor shows its lines without their first ">" function isQuoteList(u) { return u.kind === "list" && u.tag === "blockquote"; } function unquote(source) { return source.split(/\r?\n/).map(function(line) { return line.replace(/^>[ \t]?/, ""); }).join("\n"); } // Edited lines back into > lines: a ">" in front ("> " before text, ">" before a deeper marker); blank lines go function quote(source, nl) { return source.split(/\r?\n/).filter(function(line) { return /\S/.test(line); }).map(function(line) { return (outlineModel.MARKER_CHARS.indexOf(line.charAt(0)) !== -1 ? ">" : "> ") + line; }).join(nl); } // Replace the unit's content (see contentStart, fenced, isQuoteList) with newSource exports.replace = function(text, model, id, newSource) { var u = model.units[id]; if(!u) { return null; } var nl = utils.eol(text), f = fenced(text, u); if(f) { return {text: utils.splice(text, u.start, u.end, f.open + nl + newSource + nl + f.close), select: u.start}; } if(isQuoteList(u)) { return {text: utils.splice(text, u.start, u.end, quote(newSource, nl)), select: u.start}; } newSource = stripTypedMarker(u, newSource); if(isOneLine(u)) { newSource = toBreaks(newSource); } return {text: utils.splice(text, contentStart(text, u), u.end, newSource), select: u.start}; }; /* Insert a new sibling unit (item) or first block (heading/block) after unit `id`, or, `where` "before", in front of it (an item: a sibling with its marker; anything else: a paragraph); null for blank source. A new item's text that starts with the item's own marker and a space (typed out of habit) loses that marker: it is added anyway. */ exports.insertNew = function(text, model, id, newSource, marker, where) { var u = model.units[id]; newSource = u ? stripTypedMarker(u, newSource) : newSource; if(!u || !newSource || !newSource.trim()) { return null; } var nl = utils.eol(text), pos, insert, select; if(u.kind === "item" && where === "before") { pos = u.start; insert = u.marker + " " + toBreaks(newSource) + nl; select = pos; } else if(u.kind === "item") { pos = u.subtreeEnd; insert = nl + (marker || u.marker) + " " + toBreaks(newSource); select = pos + nl.length; } else if(where === "before") { return insertBlockBefore(text, u, newSource); } else { return insertBlockAt(text, u.end, newSource); } return {text: utils.splice(text, pos, pos, insert), select: select}; }; /* Marker of a new item after item `id` (insertNew), `delta` levels deeper (Tab) or higher (negative, Shift-Tab) than the item: one more of the item's last marker character per level deeper, one character less per level higher. Null when out of range: above depth 1, or more than one level below the last item of the item's subtree (the new item would have no parent). */ exports.newItemMarker = function(model, id, delta) { var u = model.units[id]; if(!u || u.kind !== "item") { return null; } var items = subtreeUnits(model, u, "item"), last = items[items.length - 1]; var length = u.marker.length + delta; if(length < 1 || length > last.marker.length + 1) { return null; } return delta > 0 ? u.marker + u.marker.charAt(u.marker.length - 1).repeat(delta) : u.marker.substring(0, length); }; // Insert block `source` at `pos` (end of a unit), set apart by a blank line before and, when content follows, after function insertBlockAt(text, pos, source) { var nl = utils.eol(text), insert = nl + nl + source, rest = text.substring(pos); if(/\S/.test(rest) && !/^\r?\n[ \t]*\r?\n/.test(rest)) { insert += nl; } return {text: utils.splice(text, pos, pos, insert), select: pos + 2 * nl.length}; } // Insert block `source` in front of unit `u`, set apart by blank lines (it ends the section above) function insertBlockBefore(text, u, source) { var nl = utils.eol(text), before = text.substring(0, u.start), lead = !/\S/.test(before) || /\n[ \t]*\r?\n[ \t]*$/.test(before) ? "" : (/\n[ \t]*$/.test(before) ? nl : nl + nl); return {text: utils.splice(text, u.start, u.start, lead + source + nl + nl), select: u.start + lead.length}; } /* Block types of the block menu (Alt-Enter): the unit kind they produce and their source from content (line breaks `nl`). Headings, list items and quote lines are one source line: their line breaks become <br>. */ var BLOCK_TYPES = { paragraph: {kind: "block", make: function(c) { return c; }}, heading1: {kind: "heading", make: function(c) { return "! " + toBreaks(c); }}, heading2: {kind: "heading", make: function(c) { return "!! " + toBreaks(c); }}, heading3: {kind: "heading", make: function(c) { return "!!! " + toBreaks(c); }}, bulleted: {kind: "item", make: function(c) { return "* " + toBreaks(c); }}, numbered: {kind: "item", make: function(c) { return "# " + toBreaks(c); }}, quote: {kind: "item", make: function(c) { return "> " + toBreaks(c); }}, code: {kind: "block", make: function(c, nl) { return "```" + nl + c + nl + "```"; }} }; // Unit kind a block type produces ("item" for list types), or null exports.blockTypeKind = function(type) { return BLOCK_TYPES[type] ? BLOCK_TYPES[type].kind : null; }; /* Where insertBlock puts a new block of `type` after unit `id`: right after a heading's own line for a non-heading block (it becomes the first block of the section), otherwise after the unit's whole subtree. */ exports.insertsAfterSubtree = function(model, id, type) { var u = model.units[id]; return !!u && !(u.kind === "heading" && exports.blockTypeKind(type) !== "heading"); }; /* Insert a new block of `type` with `content`. `where`: "after" (default) unit `id` (see insertsAfterSubtree), "before" it (it ends the section above), or "end" of the text (`id` is ignored: the first block of an empty tiddler). Not next to a single list item. Null for blank content. */ exports.insertBlock = function(text, model, id, type, content, where) { var u = model.units[id], t = BLOCK_TYPES[type]; if(!t || !content || !content.trim()) { return null; } var nl = utils.eol(text), result; content = content.replace(/\r?\n/g, nl); if(where === "end") { var head = text.replace(/\s+$/, ""), prefix = /\S/.test(head) ? head + nl + nl : ""; result = {text: prefix + t.make(content, nl), select: prefix.length}; } else if(!u || u.kind === "item") { return null; } else if(where === "before") { result = insertBlockBefore(text, u, t.make(content, nl)); } else { result = insertBlockAt(text, exports.insertsAfterSubtree(model, id, type) ? u.subtreeEnd : u.end, t.make(content, nl)); } result.kind = t.kind; return result; }; // Content of a paragraph, heading or code block (line breaks as \n, <br> of headings too), or null for other units function blockContent(text, u) { if(u.kind === "heading") { return text.substring(contentStart(text, u), u.end).replace(/<br\s*\/?>/gi, "\n"); } if(u.kind !== "block") { return null; } var source = text.substring(u.start, u.end).replace(/\r\n/g, "\n"); if(u.tag === "p") { return source; } var f = u.tag === "codeblock" ? fenced(text, u) : null; return f ? f.content : null; } /* The "Turn into" types offered for unit `id`: a bullet switches between bulleted and numbered, a whole list too; paragraphs, headings and code blocks turn into the other block types. The current type is left out. */ exports.convertTypes = function(model, id) { var u = model.units[id]; if(!u) { return []; } if(u.kind === "item") { var last = u.marker.charAt(u.marker.length - 1); return last === "*" ? ["numbered"] : last === "#" ? ["bulleted"] : []; } if(u.kind === "list") { return u.tag === "ul" ? ["numbered"] : u.tag === "ol" ? ["bulleted"] : []; } var text = model.text; if(blockContent(text, u) === null) { return []; } var all = u.tag === "codeblock" ? "" : this.units[id].unit.kind); // Same text (e.g. two identical siblings swapped): no write, but the frame still follows result.select if(!old || result.text !== (old.fields.text || "")) { this.writeText(old, result.text); } this.saveSelection(result.select, id === -1 ? 0 : id, kind); return true; }; methods.isReadOnly = function() { return this.wiki.getTiddlerText(READ_ONLY) === "yes"; }; /* ---------- events ---------- */ methods.handleKeydown = function(event) { // Consumed elsewhere (AutoComplete popups listen in the capture phase), or from an element inside if(event.defaultPrevented || event.target !== this.domNode) { return; } // An open block menu takes its keys; any other key closes it and acts as usual if(this.menu) { if(this.handleMenuKeydown(event)) { event.preventDefault(); event.stopPropagation(); return; } this.closeMenu(); } // An open key overview closes with Escape before Escape clears the selection if(event.keyCode === 27 && !event.ctrlKey && !event.altKey && !event.metaKey && !event.shiftKey && this.isHelpOpen()) { this.toggleHelp(false); event.preventDefault(); event.stopPropagation(); return; } for(var i = 0; i < ACTIONS.length; i++) { var action = ACTIONS[i]; if((this.keyMatches(event, action.name) || typedChar(event, action.char)) && action.run(this)) { event.preventDefault(); event.stopPropagation(); return; } } }; function typedChar(event, ch) { return !!ch && event.key === ch && !event.ctrlKey && !event.altKey && !event.metaKey; } /* ---------- key overview ---------- */ // The overview (ui/keys-table) is shown by the body template while this temp tiddler is "yes" methods.helpTitle = function() { return HELP_PREFIX + this.tiddlerTitle; }; methods.isHelpOpen = function() { return this.wiki.getTiddlerText(this.helpTitle()) === "yes"; }; // Open, close (open = true/false) or toggle the key overview. Outline Work on an ordinary tiddler like on a Streams outline: select a block, edit it in place, move it with Alt-Up/Down, indent it with Tab, and see the result rendered at once. The tiddler stays one tiddler; no helper tiddlers are created. !! Features * ''Toggle per tiddler'' — an //outline// button in the view toolbar. Off means the normal view, with no extra handlers. * ''Same rendering'' — the tiddler renders exactly as usual. Outline mode only adds data attributes, a selection frame and key handling. * ''Units'' — list items, lists, headings (with their sections), paragraphs, code blocks, tables, opened HTML containers, transclusion lines, and widgets or macro calls (one opaque unit each). * ''Type badges'' — a small, faint label next to every unit shows what it is (paragraph, h2, code-block, bullet, ...), also on the editor field; they take no space. Settings: all (default), headings only, off. * ''Selection'' — click, Up/Down in document order, Left/Right to the parent / first child, Escape clears. * ''Move'' — Alt-Up/Alt-Down swap a unit with its sibling, carrying its subtree. Headings and blocks also move across heading lines: a new heading moves up over the blocks above it, a paragraph moves into the next section. * ''Indent'' — Tab/Shift-Tab demote/promote list items (one marker character) and headings (one `!`) with their subtrees. * ''In-place editor'' — Enter or a double-click opens TW's own edit widget at the unit (AutoComplete and other editor plugins work): a compact one-line field by default, optionally the full editor with toolbar. Lists and headings are edited without their marker; nesting stays with Tab/Shift-Tab. Ctrl-Enter saves, Enter saves and starts a new unit, Escape discards, Ctrl-Up/Down save and move the editor to the previous/next unit, Alt-Enter turns the unit into another type. In selection mode Ctrl-Enter starts a new empty unit below the selection. * ''Delete'' — the Delete key removes the selection with everything below it, after a small yes/no menu (a heading: with its section or just the heading); list items without sub-items go at once (a setting). * ''Copy, cut, paste'' — Ctrl-C, Ctrl-X, Ctrl-V move a unit with its subtree, also to another tiddler; through the system clipboard: formatted into e-mail or Jira, as wikitext into text fields; pasted into an outline a unit takes the level of the place. * ''Undo'' — Ctrl-Z takes back the last changes made in the outline (deletes, moves, merges, splits, edits), Ctrl-Y redoes them; for the running session. In the editor too, as long as nothing is typed (after a split, merge or move from the editor). * ''Split and merge'' — Enter in the middle of a list item splits it at the caret, at the start of a filled item or paragraph it opens an empty one above; Backspace at the start of an item joins it to the item above (an empty item is deleted), Delete at its end pulls the item below up, like in Streams. * ''Block menu'' — Alt-Enter (also in the editor, to turn the edited unit into another type): insert a new paragraph, heading, list, quote or code block after or before the selection (in an empty tiddler: the first block), or turn the selection into another type (a bullet list into a numbered one, a paragraph into a heading, ...). * ''Key overview'' — press `?` in an outline (or its small ? button) for a table of all keys; the //keys// tab shows the same. Every key is configurable in the settings tab with TW's shortcut editor. * ''Transclusions'' — a small marker on `{{…}}` lines; Enter opens the target in outline mode. * ''Safe writes'' — every write is a splice of a known range; if the text changed underneath, the edit is relocated or refused, never guessed. !! Prerequisites * TiddlyWiki 5.4.0 or later (JS modules: server restart or reload needed after install) * Optional: `rimir/theme` (`rr-` styles in settings), `rimir/doc-template` (branded docs) !! Quick Start # Install the plugin and restart the server (the widget and key modules load only at startup). # Open a wikitext tiddler and press //outline// in its view toolbar. # Click a block. Move with Up/Down, press Alt-Down to move it below its sibling, Tab to indent it. # Press Enter, change the text, press Ctrl-Enter to save. # Press `?` to see all keys. Wikitext only; Markdown tiddlers are not supported yet.
